podcast.title: Band Decline (1986)
podcast.body: By 1986, Missing Persons began to fall apart, coinciding with Warren Cuccurullo's opportunity to join Duran Duran. "But then in 1986, Missing Persons was falling apart."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Early Success (1980s)
podcast.body: Missing Persons was formed in 1980 by Warren Cuccurullo, Tony Bozzio (a former Frank Zappa drummer), and Tony's wife, Dale Bozzio, who had also contributed to Zappa's work. The band found success with several new wave hits, becoming a staple on MTV in the early 1980s. Dale Bozzio, the singer, was known for her uninhibited persona, which included performing nude photo shoots for Hustler magazine in both 1979 and 1980. "Missing Persons had several new wavehids that made them an MTV stable for a while in the early 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Courtney Love's Missing Person Report Allegation (April 4, 1994)
xref.body: Tom Grant claims that on April 4, 1994, Courtney Love filed a missing person's report for Kurt, impersonating his mother, Wendy Cobain. The report stated, "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal," a wording that Grant believes was intentionally crafted to frame Kurt's subsequent death as a suicide, guiding the police investigation towards that conclusion. "It was Courtney that called that report in. I believe one of the reasons she did that in my own personal opinion is so that she could word the report because the wording on that missing persons report turned out to be a pretty important thing in this investigation."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: False Missing Persons Report (1994)
xref.body: On Monday, April 4, 1994, Courtney Love filed a missing persons report for Kurt Cobain, falsely identifying herself as Kurt's mother, Wendy Cobain. Tom Grant believed she did this to control the report's wording, which stated Kurt "ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal." "On Monday April 4th she called in a missing persons report and she pretended to be Kurt's mother Wendy Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Missing Persons Report & Detective Search (April 1994)
xref.body: Courtney Love, frantic and fearing Kurt would harm himself, hired an LA detective named Tom Grant to track him down. Kurt's mother also filed a missing persons report with the Seattle police. "She hired an LA detective named Tom Grant to track him down. His mother filed a missing persons report with the Seattle police."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Missing Persons Report (1994)
xref.body: On Monday, April 4, 1994, a missing persons report for Kurt Cobain was filed. Courtney Love, his wife, made this call, pretending to be Kurt's mother, Wendy Cobain. "It was Courtney that called that report in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Wording of Missing Persons Report (1994)
xref.body: The missing persons report filed for Kurt Cobain was worded as follows: "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal." This wording became a critical point in later investigations, particularly as it seemed to pre-emptively suggest the circumstances of his death. "Mr. Cobain ran away from California facility and flew back to Seattle. He also body shotgun and maybe suicidal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Multiple Police Stops in Arkansas
xref.body: After going missing from Texas, Leila and Ray Howard were pulled over twice by different cops in rural Arkansas on July 2nd. The first stop was for Leila driving with her headlights off, where the trooper noted they were polite but heading in the wrong direction, and Leila seemed to remember their home address. Half an hour later, they were stopped again for driving with high beams on. In both instances, they were let go with a warning, as neither officer realized they were dealing with missing persons. "Neither cop had any idea that they were dealing with a couple of missing persons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
